# Quench

> JavaScript, TypeScript and WebAssembly runtime written in Rust. Test262: 53,353 passing, 0 failing. Interpreter, two JITs, and AOT to native executables.

Quench runs TypeScript, JavaScript and WebAssembly with Node-compatible APIs. Its engine is entirely Rust: OXC parser, register-bytecode interpreter, b-jit (copy-and-patch JIT), u-jit (Cranelift JIT) and an AOT compiler that produces native executables. All tiers derive from one shared definition of each opcode. MIT licensed. Early: no packaged releases, build from source with Cargo, Linux.

Key measured facts (interpreter only in every engine: quench --no-jit, node --jitless, Bun with BUN_JSC_useJIT=0; one 4-core Linux machine):
- V8-v7, 14 Nov 2026: Quench scores 1.49x to 2.57x the faster of Node and Bun on all 8 benchmarks; peak memory 0.28x to 0.55x of the smaller on 7 of 8 (splay 1.07x).
- JetStream 3, 17 Nov 2026, 56 tests all three finish: score 34.3 (Node 39.7, Bun 32.2); peak memory 28.5 MB (Node 110.1 MB, Bun 47.7 MB).
- Test262: 53,353 passing, 0 failing, 53 waived (Node-identical failures, still counted as failures). WebAssembly spec: 67,124 of 67,124.
- AOT, 25 Nov 2026: quench compile --strict-aot evaluates a program at build time up to its first run-time input. Hello world compiles to a 4,896-byte executable, 0.96 ms startup, 1.3 MB peak RSS (C: 14 KB, 0.89 ms, 1.36 MB; Node 22: 27.5 ms, 36 MB). Programs that read input fall back to a full image (readline REPL: 71.3 MB, 6.2 ms, 4.42 MB); shrinking that is in progress.
- V8 v7, 25 Nov 2026 (commit 37fbb34909), geomean of 8: no-jit 2,986 vs Node --jitless 2,098 / Bun no-JIT 1,675 (1.42x), peak RSS 11.0 MB vs 24.7 MB (0.45x). JIT on (Quench default): 3,222 vs Node 25,093 / Bun 32,514 (0.10x), 27.2 MB vs 51.6 MB (0.53x). Target in every mode: 1.5x score at 0.5x RSS.
- TypeScript types are never erased: annotations (and JSDoc in JavaScript) become facts checked once and trusted by every tier.
- Native hot module replacement: quench --hmr app.ts; import.meta.hot / module.hot accept, dispose, decline, invalidate; unaccepted edits restart the process.
- Daily progress posts: https://quench.run/blog/ (feed https://quench.run/blog/feed.xml)
- Weak spots: cold code loading, async/promises, proxies; JIT tiers not yet competitive; no AOT compute speed numbers published; Deno not measured.

## Built for agent Code Mode
Quench targets agent harnesses that run model-written code in-process (Code Mode), often hundreds of agents per machine:
- The QuickJS slot, with more speed: small, embedded, interpreter only. With the JIT off, V8-v7 scores 1.49x to 2.57x (14 Nov 2026) the best of node --jitless and Bun; five of eight benchmarks peak at 6.4 to 8.2 MB RSS (Node 43 to 50 MB, Bun 16 to 26 MB). Not yet benchmarked against QuickJS; that is a positioning goal, not a result.
- Embeddable and Rust-native: quench-runtime is a Rust library (Runtime with a Host, host functions for tools, execution interrupt to stop runaway code). Not on crates.io yet; API unstable.
- No JIT required: --no-jit (the library default) runs the interpreter only, WebAssembly included; no machine code is generated at run time, removing JIT-compiler bugs from the attack surface. Not a sandbox by itself; isolation comes from the host.
- Full JavaScript and TypeScript: Test262 53,353 passing, 0 failing; TypeScript runs without a build step; node: APIs.
- Page: https://quench.run/javascript-engine-for-ai-agents/
